stem.text: A particle moves along the curve \( x y^{2} = 12 \) so that its coordinates \( x \) and \( y \) are differentiable functions of time \( t \). At the instant the particle is at the point \( (3, 2) \), the \( y \)-coordinate of the particle is decreasing at a rate of 1 unit per second. Find \( \frac{dx}{dt} \), in units per second, at that instant.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate both sides of \( x y^{2} = 12 \) with respect to \( t \), using the product rule on the term that contains both variables: \( \left(y^{2}\right)\frac{dx}{dt} + \left(2 x y\right)\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \).
At \( (3, 2) \) the coefficient of \( \frac{dy}{dt} \) is \( 12 \) and the coefficient of \( \frac{dx}{dt} \) is \( 4 \). Substitute \( \frac{dy}{dt} = -1 \): \( (12)(-1) + (4)\frac{dx}{dt} = 0 \).
